Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Goal 2 Core Concepts 2.1 Cards 2.2 Magic Stones 2.3 Points 3 Hunting Phase 4 Turn 5 Resolution Phase 6 Game End Goal Score 60 points at the end of a round or have the the most points at the end of round 10 by summoning creatures from your hand Core Concepts Cards There is no hand limit. The maximum number of cards a player can have in their summoning area is equal to the current round. Additional spots are added every round, cards may also be removed from the summoning area by spending magic stones. A card has a family, which determines how much it can be sold for and other effects. Card images can be seen at higher resolution at https://valeofeternity.wiki.gg/wiki/All_Cards . Each card has one of 3 types of effect: Instant (lightning bolt ⚡︎ ): Triggers only when the card is being summoned. Permanent (infinity ∞): Activates always after the card has been summoned. Active (hourglass ⌛︎ ): Activates once per round during the Resolution Phase. Magic Stones Magic Stones are the currency used to summon and remove cards. A Red Stone is worth 1, a Blue Stone is worth 3, a Purple Stone is worth 6. Magic stones are limited to a quantity of 4 regardless of their value (e.g. 4 red 1s or 4 purple 6s). If a player exceeds this limit, they must keep 4 magic stones and discard the rest. This decision must be made before taking any other actions. Magic Stones cannot be freely traded to make room for others, e.g. if you have 4 red 1s, you cannot trade 3 of them for 1 blue 3. If a player overspends their magic stones, they cannot make change e.g. using a purple 6 for something that costs 4 does not grant you 2 red 1s back. Points Due to various effects, players can gain or lose points throughout the game, although minimum score at any time is 0 (i.e. no negatives). The Game ends when a player has 60 points at the end of a round or at the end of the 10th round. Hunting Phase To start the round, each player drafts two cards First card is drafted clockwise from start player, second card is drafted anticlockwise from last player (this means the last player drafts both their cards at once essentially) Turn On your turn, you take as many of the actions as many times as desired After all players have done this, the action phase ends The actions are: Sell, Tame, Summon, Remove Sell - Pick a card you chose during the Hunting Phase and discard it, receive Magic Stones based on its family (this is NOT its cost). Red Fire gives 3 Red Stones, Blue Water gives 1 Blue Stones, Green Earth gives 4 Red Stones, Pink Wind gives 1 Red & 1 Blue stone, Purple Dragon gives 1 Purple Stone Sell Value by Family Family Sell For Value Total Stones Fire 3 Red Magic Stones 3 3 Earth 4 Red Magic Stones 4 4 Water 1 Blue Magic Stone 3 1 Wind 1 Red Magic Stone 1 Blue Magic Stone 4 2 Dragon 1 Purple Magic Stone 6 1 Tame - Pick a card you chose during the Hunting Phase and put it into your hand Summon - If you have open areas, you may pay the cost of a card and place it into your playing area, this cost may be reduced by the effect of cards already in your playing area. After which, resolve any instant effects if it has one. Remove - You may remove a card from your own playing area at the cost of the current round, e.g. in round 6 the cost is 6 Resolution Phase In turn order, each player can activate each active effect on their cards in their playing area once each, in any order. Card effects must be used if player meets the card criteria. Recover is a keyword that puts a summoned card back in the owner’s hand. If no specific target is described, the card recovers itself.

[Rating: 1/10] Far from an expert as I've only played this a few times, but in that small handful of plays it was apparent that the card powers were not appropriately balanced—some are significantly and clearly better than others—and the random way in which they come out means one might get totally screwed through no fault of their own and with no real way to get back into the fight. Outside of that, I don't love the SPLENDOR-based ladder climbing of "cards earn resources which allow you to get better cards that are then worth points". Like chasing your own tail.

[Rating: 1/10] The card abilities are extremely unbalanced. The skills and attributes of some characters or cards are overly powerful, while others are relatively weak. Moreover, the abilities are overly fancy and not closely connected to the theme. It feels like they are forced into the game unnaturally. Apart from the relatively beautiful card face designs, there are no other merits.

[Rating: 2/10] To much downtime. Because you have to check every round which cards can be select and which ability they have.

[Rating: 3/10] Luck-fest. But some minor charming elements. 2 minute rules. Too long for what it offers (but I guess I can see why it needs to be that long cause otherwise the randomness gets even more annoying... probably).  And the negative interaction cards have no place in a game like this. Especially at anything other than 2p.

[Rating: 3/10] This type of game is really not to my taste, but I bet some people will really like this. I think that Fantasy Realms does what VoE wants to do but in less time and with less rules, and as usual, Race for the Galaxy is better.   The pentagonal market is dumb.

The lack of options in the card offer (two for each player) and the fact that good cards just might not come out when you're early in player order makes playing simultaneously boring and infuriating.
